text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The AEX share index could be heading down to 780 points, around 70 points below the current level, according to a Reuter poll. The poll, which asked analysts around the world about trends in their markets, tapped 120 analysts in 14 countries. (p1)
- Youth unemployment falls by around a third over the year. During March to May unemployment in this sector was 5.6 percent, the lowest level in the last 10 years, government says. (p1)

- Enertel, a consortium of Dutch cable and energy companies aiming to offer telephony services, lodges complaint with telecoms ministry about rival PTT Telecom's rates for third party access to its telecoms network. (p1) VOLKSKRANT
- Vitatron, which makes pacemakers, wants to transfer a part of its production abroad in two years' time. Around 130 of the 250 jobs might be involved. (p31)
- The Dutch trades unions federation calls for "golden handshakes" for every worker made redundant. (p31)
- Retailers can only offer promotions in stores for a maximum of eight weeks after the government defines limits for the first time. (p31) DE TELEGRAAF
- Dairy equipment manufacturer Prolion plans to issue new shares on the New Market of the Amsterdam bourse. (p33)
- Dutch businesses loses hundreds of millions of guilders because automation projects are often not define clearly enough. (p33)
- U.S. energy and chemicals business Ashland chooses Rotterdam as European centre. (p33) ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- The AEX index is set to fall to 780 or 800 in July or August, according to a private investors' club. (p11)
- Dutch business is underestimating the impact the new millennium will have on automised systems. (p11)
